answer.market_read: Our shop is 1st among shops (ALL 0.951, revenue 2nd, book 3rd). Class rank is 6 at 1.487 against inextro 1.719, and the gap is almost all buyer ALL (0.565). Following the user's priority, shop moves this round protect book and free cash; they do not chase revenue rank. Cash is 44.6M against 442M of stock (inextro 135M), so storage at ~1%/day costs us about 4.4M of book a day, and the cheapest book gain is shrinking piles that turn slowly or earn thin margin. Three engines need no moves: Mate 4-seat (150 sold/6h, 0.3h hold), Plana 4 swing (24/6h, 434k/unit, 3 shops) and Ace BMA, all pinned or clearing fast. The aged piles are Zinus Lumi (33 units, 10.9h old, 9 sold/6h, already at the 0.85 ask floor and cover 0.25), Simmons Hub (10 units, 7.2h, 5/6h) and the GS loess sofa (8.9h). The low-margin crowded piles are Zinus Ultima SS (55 units, 11% margin, 17 shops, ~6h of our sales), Zinus Cloud (60 units, walk-aways 77 vs sold 53, market paid 0.61-0.73) and the mattress pad (113 units, surge 1.104). Recent cover-cut predictions overshot by about 2x (Lumi predicted 30 and got 12, then 20 and got 9), so I predict cuts at ~35% of last-6h sales. Stock-0 raises missed again (Avenuel Shrunken, Plana Basic 3, Sealy, GS sofa), so stock-0 lines stay untouched (L3). The cash freed goes to small, cheap, fast-clearing lines with few shops and 12-18% margin: the folding mattress, vegan duvet and drawer chest. Apples are at surge 1.174 and stay held under L7. Plana 3 is aging (4.3h) at ask 1.04 while competitors open at 0.75, so it gets a 5% ask trim.

moves.why: Zinus Lumi: 33 units at 10.9h, 9 sold/6h, ask at the 0.85 floor and cover already 0.25. The pile holds ~22h of our sales. Stop buying and let it drain to free cash and cut storage.
Simmons Hub: 10 units at 7.2h, 5 sold/6h, ask already at the 0.85 floor (effective ~0.77, top of the 0.72-0.77 band). Only cover is left to cut.
Zinus Ultima SS: 55 units (~6h of sales), oldest 5.2h, 32k/unit (11%), 17 shops, walk-aways 89 vs sold 56. A crowded thin-margin pile is the best cash source; no price cut (L5).
Zinus Cloud: 60 units (~6.8h of sales), walk-aways 77 vs sold 53, market paid 0.61-0.73 with the cheapest shop at 0.61. Trim the pile rather than cut an 11.6% margin.
Mattress pad: 113 units (~5.8h of sales) at surge 1.104. Further buying raises our own unit cost, so hold the pile size down.
GS loess sofa G208SF: oldest 8.9h, 12 shops, ~10% margin. Do not refill an aged thin-margin line.
Plana 3: oldest 4.3h, 16 units, ask 1.04 while competitor first asks sit at 0.75 median. At 353k/unit, a 5% trim keeps margin and slows aging.
Folding mattress: 0.1h hold, sold-out asks, only 4 shops, 37 sold/6h on 10 units, 12.5% margin, low cost per unit. Cheap to fund from the cuts above.
Vegan goose duvet: 0.5h hold, 5 shops, 20 sold/6h on 11 units, ~18% margin, 209k list.
Borneo drawer chest: 17 sold/6h on 6 units, 5 shops, 12.5% margin, unserved storage-furniture orders. Small cash outlay.

lessons.text: Cover cuts on piles holding more than 6h of our own sales free cash reliably, but sales also slow. Predict sold_next_6h at about 35% of last 6h, or about 25% if our ask sits above the market's settle band (sku_prices). Measured: Lumi predicted 30 and got 12, predicted 20 and got 9.
lessons.why: Cover-cut predictions at 50% overshot twice on Lumi; the median outcome was ~40% of the prediction.

lessons.text: With the buyer score first (11-06), each round spend cash from crowded thin-margin piles (15+ shops, margin <12%) on cheap fast-clearing lines with few shops (<=5) and margin 12-20%. Keep big-ticket pinned engines untouched.
lessons.why: This protects book without speculative stock-0 raises, which keep missing.

Mattress pad cost climbing; cut cover further or raise the ask.
